facts.statement: The genus was described in 2005 by a team led by paleontologist Stéphane Jouve.
facts.quote: described in 2005 by a team led by palaeontologist Stéphane Jouve

facts.statement: Four specimens have been described by Stéphane Jouve and colleagues.
facts.quote: Four specimens have been described by Stéphane Jouve and colleagues

facts.statement: All described specimens come from the Sidi Chenane phosphate mine.
facts.quote: All of them stem from the Sidi Chenane phosphate mine

facts.statement: The genus is named after French paleontologist Camille Arambourg in recognition of his research on Morocco's phosphate mine fossils.
facts.quote: Arambourgisuchus is named after French paleontologist Camille Arambourg for his research on the fossil fauna of Morocco's phosphate mines

facts.statement: The species name refers to the town of Khouribga, located north of the type locality.
facts.quote: The species name alludes to the town of Khouribga north of the type locality

facts.statement: Arambourgisuchus lived during the Thanetian age of the Paleocene, approximately 59 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: the deposits yielding Arambourgisuchus dating to the Thanetian age of the Paleocene, ca. 59 to 56 Ma

facts.statement: The skull measures up to 1 meter in length, with most of that length consisting of the elongated snout.
facts.quote: The skull of Arambourgisuchus measures up to 1 m in length, most of which being made up by the elongated rostrum

facts.statement: The teeth are generally robust and sharp.
facts.quote: The teeth of Arambourgisuchus are generally robust and sharp

facts.statement: The long and narrow maxilla makes up the majority of the snout, giving the animal a longirostrine appearance.
facts.quote: The maxilla is long and narrow, making up the majority of the rostrum and gives the dyrosaur its longirostrine appearance

facts.statement: Like other dyrosaurids, it was a marine predator.
facts.quote: Como otros dirosáuridos, se trataba de un depredador marino

facts.statement: Its teeth were sharp, strong, and large, but fewer in number than those of Dyrosaurus phosphaticus.
facts.quote: Sus dientes eran afilados pero fuertes y grandes, así como menos numerosos que los de Dyrosaurus phosphaticus

facts.statement: The genus authority is Jouve et al., 2005, and the type species is Arambourgisuchus khouribgaensis.
facts.quote: taxon: Arambourgisuchus authority: Jouve et al., 2005 type_species: Arambourgisuchus khouribgaensis type_species_authority: Jouve et al., 2005

facts.statement: Arambourgisuchus belongs to the family Dyrosauridae.
It is classified as a member of Dyrosauridae based on large occipital tuberosities and a supratemporal fenestra that is longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: Arambourgisuchus khourbgaensis es un miembro de Dyrosauridae, basándose en la presencia de las siguientes sinapomorfias: Presencia de grandes tuberosidades occipitales Fenestra supratemporal más larga que ancha

facts.statement: The lack of better material makes a correct determination of its affinities difficult.
facts.quote: la carencia de mejores materiales hace dificultosa una correcta determinación de sus afinidades
